diagnostic_criteria: Fasting Plasma Glucose >= 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) after minimum 8-hour fast
Two-hour post-load glucose >= 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) during Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT)
HbA1c >= 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) standardized to NGSP assay
Random plasma glucose >= 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) in presence of classic osmotic symptoms
recommended_investigations: Fasting and 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose at baseline and follow-up
Quarterly HbA1c testing until glycemic target is stabilized, then biannually
Baseline serum creatinine, blood urea, and calculated eGFR
Annual spot urine for Microalbumin/Creatinine ratio (UACR)
Fasting lipid profile (Total Cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, Triglycerides) annually
Annual dilated retinal examination by ophthalmologist
Comprehensive foot examination including 10g monofilament and vibration sense
lifestyle_precautions: Medical Nutrition Therapy: 50-60% calories from complex unrefined carbohydrates with low glycemic index
Restrict dietary saturated fats to <7% and eliminate trans-fatty acids
Increase dietary soluble fiber to >30 g/day through legumes, pulses, and green vegetables
150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity (e.g., brisk walking, cycling)
Target 5-7% weight reduction in overweight or obese patients
Strict cessation of all tobacco and smoking products

medicines.name: Metformin Hydrochloride
medicines.notes: Initiate at 500 mg once or twice daily with meals; titrate gradually up to 2000 mg/day as tolerated. Contraindicated if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m².

medicines.name: Glimepiride
medicines.purpose: Second-line Sulfonylurea secretagogue for dual oral therapy
medicines.notes: 1 mg to 2 mg once daily before breakfast. Counsel patient regarding signs of hypoglycemia.

medicines.name: Teneligliptin
medicines.purpose: DPP-4 Inhibitor for glycemic control without hypoglycemia risk
medicines.notes: 20 mg once daily with or without food. Suitable across renal impairment stages.

medicines.name: Dapagliflozin / Empagliflozin
medicines.purpose: SGLT2 Inhibitor with cardiorenal protective benefit
medicines.notes: 10 mg once daily. Ensure adequate hydration; monitor for mycotic genital infections.

red_flags_refer_to_doctor: Severe hypoglycemia episodes (< 54 mg/dL) with confusion or loss of consciousness
Suspected Diabetic Ketoacidosis: persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, Kussmaul breathing, ketones in urine
Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State: blood glucose > 600 mg/dL with severe dehydration
Active diabetic foot ulcer, gangrene, or rapidly spreading soft tissue infection
Rapid decline in renal function or persistent heavy proteinuria
follow_up: Self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) per individualized schedule
HbA1c evaluation every 3 months until target (< 7.0%) achieved, then every 6 months
Clinical review of blood pressure, weight, and treatment adherence every 1-3 months
Annual screening for nephropathy, retinopathy, and peripheral neuropathy
